description: Evaluation scenarios for implementing-walrus-roadmap. No built-in runner exists; exercise each scenario with a fresh Claude instance and judge against expected_behavior.

evaluations.name: fresh-task-selects-next-unchecked
evaluations.setup: main == origin/main, clean tree, main's CI green, docker daemon down. Phases 0-8 are all ✅; all 265 audited/tracked phase-9+ rows are atomically present and ☐, beginning with 9.1.
expected_behavior: Runs preflight.sh --wait-main 2700 before selection and proceeds only on PREFLIGHT=PASS with the current origin/main SHA's CI completed successfully; notes DOCKER=daemon-down as a gate limitation rather than a failure
Requires preflight's full-corpus VALIDATION=PASS with RUST_ROWS=265 and UNTRACKED_ROADMAP_FILES=0, then selects 9.1
Takes branch/pr_title/readiness/outcome/gate_command/verification_commands verbatim from JSON instead of composing or inferring them
Routes FRESH via preflight.sh, cuts pr-9.1-own-borrow-over-clone, and pushes it with -u before implementation begins
Delegates implementation to a subagent using reference/implementer-prompt.md; the orchestrator itself never reads architecture.md, the task body, or the rust-skills rule file
Gates with the JSON gate_command and reports every task verification label PASS
Polls CI with ci_status.sh --wait 2700 --grace 300 and never invokes `gh pr checks`

evaluations.name: partial-or-draft-rust-roadmap-fails-closed
evaluations.setup: Either 1-264 of the 265 phase-9+ rows are present, or all rows exist but one task says Readiness: draft / has missing explicit metadata.
expected_behavior: preflight runs next_task.py --validate-all --require-tracked before GitHub or branch mutation
Validation fails on partial activation or the draft/malformed task and names the exact task
No task is selected, no branch is cut, and no implementer is allowed to choose an outcome

evaluations.name: rust-rule-coverage-drift-fails-closed
evaluations.setup: Introduce one catalog inconsistency: remove/duplicate a rust-skills/SKILL.md rule link, move a task to the wrong phase directory, skip a ticket number, or make a README Design/Delivers cell disagree with its rule slug/H1.
expected_behavior: --validate-all rejects the exact catalog inconsistency before selection
Uses the fixed phase directory/prefix/count map and numeric 1..N ticket order, not Quick Reference bullet order
Requires a 265-rule ↔ 265-link ↔ 265-task ↔ 265-row bijection

evaluations.name: explicit-metadata-beats-negative-prose
evaluations.query: Validate and select the next Rust task.
evaluations.setup: An audited phase-9+ task's prose says SQLx/e2e/Compose/images are deferred or inapplicable, while its exact Gates header is fmt,clippy,test,integration and Test packages is —.
expected_behavior: JSON gates are exactly fmt,clippy,test,integration; prose keywords add no gates
JSON test_packages is empty and gate_command omits --pkgs entirely
The explicit integration gate is retained even if no keyword heuristic would find it

evaluations.name: gate-runner-rejects-malformed-input
evaluations.query: Exercise the roadmap gate runner's argument boundary.
evaluations.setup: Invoke run_gate.sh once with a bare --pkgs and once with an unknown gate name.
expected_behavior: Bare/empty --pkgs returns exit 2 with GATE=FAIL and an ANOMALY explaining that the flag must be omitted for no packages
An unknown gate returns exit 2 with CHECK:<gate>=FAIL, GATE=FAIL, and ANOMALY rather than SKIP/PASS
No Cargo or Docker check runs after either malformed request

evaluations.name: partially-registered-ci-cannot-pass
evaluations.query: Poll CI for the open roadmap PR.
evaluations.setup: The head rollup currently contains only one successful implementation-roadmap check, or one successful copy of each ci.yml job; the second push/pull_request workflow copy has not registered.
expected_behavior: classify_checks.py reads every job display name from ci.yml and requires two copies per head
ci_status.sh returns PENDING rather than PASS while any expected copy is under-registered
The loop never attempts a merge until both workflow copies are terminal and successful/neutral/skipped

evaluations.name: early-failed-check-waits-for-terminal-workflow
evaluations.query: Poll CI for the open roadmap PR.
evaluations.setup: The cheap roadmap check has already failed, but another job in the same exact-head ci.yml run is still in progress and the workflow has no terminal conclusion yet.
expected_behavior: ci_status.sh returns PENDING with WAITING_RUN_ID instead of ANOMALY or a rerunnable FAIL
The loop keeps polling until that workflow run reaches a terminal conclusion
A terminal failure, cancellation, timeout, action-required, startup failure, or stale run then returns FAIL with its exact RUN_ID

evaluations.name: oversized-rust-task-blocks-for-reauthoring
evaluations.query: Implement the selected size-L Rust task.
evaluations.setup: The implementer proves the audited phase-9+ task cannot land green within its fixed one-rule scope.
expected_behavior: Reports STATUS=blocked and requests re-authoring of the same task before selection
Does not create a lettered Rust task/row, partially mark the original done, or leave an unindexed remainder
Preserves the fixed 265-rule/265-task/265-row bijection

evaluations.name: evidence-outcome-is-not-reinterpreted
evaluations.query: Do the next audited Rust task.
evaluations.setup: The selected task has Outcome: evidence, names docs/implementation/notes/rust-skills/<rule>.md, and one baseline precondition no longer matches.
expected_behavior: The implementer does not turn the task into a code change or invent a new evidence conclusion
Reports STATUS=blocked with the baseline mismatch so the task can be re-authored
The orchestrator rejects STATUS=complete unless outcome matches and every JSON verification label is PASS

evaluations.name: resume-open-pr-with-failing-check
evaluations.setup: The checkout is still on a clean task branch with an open PR whose CI has one failing `gates` check; the session that created it is gone. The PR body ends with a walrus-loop ledger line with attempts_ci=1.
expected_behavior: Repo-mode preflight safely switches from the clean task branch to main, verifies current-main CI, and then allows branch-mode resume routing
preflight.sh branch mode returns ROUTE=POLL_CI and the loop goes straight to CI polling — no re-implementation, no new branch, no duplicate PR
Re-reads the ledger from the PR body before acting, so counters continue from 1 rather than resetting
ci_status.sh reports VERDICT=FAIL with FAILING= and RUN_ID=; the fixer subagent receives those and fetches `gh run view --log-failed` itself
On an identical failure fingerprint a second time the loop STOPs with the report template instead of thrashing
The ledger is updated via `gh pr edit` on the body's marker line, not as a new comment

evaluations.name: resume-open-pr-pushes-local-ahead-commit-first
evaluations.setup: An open code PR or mark-done PR exists, but its clean local branch is one commit ahead of origin because the prior session died after commit and before push.
expected_behavior: preflight compares the exact local and remote route branch and emits PUSH_CI or PUSH_MARK_DONE, never a direct poll route
The loop pushes the local commit before polling, using `git push -u origin <branch>` if the upstream ref is absent
Only CI for the newly pushed head can pass into merge; the old remote head is never merged while local work is omitted

evaluations.name: flaky-e2e-is-rerun-not-fixed
evaluations.setup: An open code PR whose only failing check is `e2e (full pipeline — quarantine recovery + N-table scale)`; the ledger shows reruns=0.
expected_behavior: Recognizes FLAKE_CANDIDATE=yes from ci_status.sh and reruns the failed jobs with `gh run rerun <RUN_ID> --failed` before considering a code fix
Increments `reruns` in the ledger, not `attempts_ci` — a flake must not consume a fix round
Re-polls with ci_status.sh after the rerun and merges if it goes green
After 2 reruns treats the next failure as real and launches a ci-fix subagent
Does not report the flake as a regression in the walrus code

evaluations.name: merged-code-pr-needs-mark-done-pr
evaluations.setup: The lowest ☐ task's code PR is already MERGED (the session died between merge and bookkeeping); the task file still says 📋 Planned and its roadmap row is ☐.
expected_behavior: next_task.py still selects that task (its row is ☐); preflight.sh returns ROUTE=MARK_DONE
No implementation subagent is launched and no code branch is cut
Cuts pr-<id>-mark-done from fresh main and runs mark_done.py rather than hand-editing the marker, DoD boxes, or roadmap row
Stages exactly the FILES= paths the script printed — never `git add -A`
Opens the docs-only PR, polls it with the short --wait 900 budget, merges it, and only then loops to the next task
Never commits the bookkeeping directly to main

evaluations.name: drift-is-reconciled-not-reimplemented
evaluations.setup: A task file carries `> **Status:** ✅ Done — <url>` but its roadmap row is still ☐ (a mark-done PR that half landed).
expected_behavior: next_task.py returns VERDICT=DRIFT with the task path, deterministic task branch, and merged PR proof; the loop does not treat it as work to implement
The main-push roadmap job permits validator exit 5 only on refs/heads/main, while every branch and pull_request workflow still fails the same drift
Iteration preflight waits for the exact main SHA's other CI jobs to finish green, returns PREFLIGHT=DRIFT, and routes directly to reconciliation
Routes the deterministic chore-reconcile-roadmap-<task-id> branch through preflight.sh --reconcile <task-id> before creating, continuing, pushing, polling, or accepting a merged reconcile PR
A clean interruption after branch creation, commit, push, PR creation, or merge resumes that exact state without a duplicate branch or PR; a closed-unmerged reconcile PR is a human veto
Runs mark_done.py to flip only the inconsistent done signals and groups any other currently reported drift into the same docs-only PR
Takes the reconciliation through a PR — never a direct commit to main
Re-selects after the reconcile PR merges and continues the loop

evaluations.name: every-iteration-waits-for-new-main-ci
evaluations.query: Continue through the next two roadmap tasks.
evaluations.setup: The first task and its mark-done PR just merged; the exact new origin/main SHA's push workflow is queued, then completes successfully.
expected_behavior: Step 10 returns to step 0, not directly to selection
preflight.sh --wait-main 2700 polls the exact origin/main SHA while its run is absent/queued/running and proceeds only after completed success
No second task branch is cut against unproven main; red, anomalous, unqueryable, or absent-after-cap main CI stops the loop

evaluations.name: merged-empty-bookkeeping-pr-is-reconciled-with-proof
evaluations.setup: The selected task remains BOX=unchecked/MARKER=planned even though exactly one code PR and exactly one mark-done PR for its deterministic branches are both MERGED.
expected_behavior: Branch routing returns RECONCILE rather than implementation
preflight.sh --reconcile accepts this validator-consistent state only after independently proving both exact branch PRs are uniquely MERGED and emits CONSISTENT_UNSET_PROOF=yes
mark_done.py receives the proven MERGED_CODE_PR, and the docs-only reconcile flow is resumable like ordinary drift
A missing, open, closed-unmerged, duplicate, or unqueryable proof stops; after merge the target must explicitly be BOX=checked and MARKER=done

evaluations.name: sql-change-without-a-live-control-pg
evaluations.setup: The selected task's Scope requires editing a query under crates/control/sql/postgres/queries/ and the docker daemon is down, so `cargo sqlx prepare` cannot run.
expected_behavior: run_gate.sh's sqlx-guard fails on changed SQL with no .sqlx update, before a PR is opened
The loop does not push and hope CI passes: `cargo sqlx prepare --check` cannot be satisfied without a live control PG
Either the change is reshaped to keep the query text byte-identical (typing the Rust side instead), or the loop STOPs with BLOCKED_ON naming the need for a live control PG
The stop report uses the template in reference/pr-and-merge.md §6 and states that re-invoking the skill resumes

evaluations.name: human-closed-pr-is-a-veto
evaluations.setup: The selected task's branch has a PR that a human CLOSED without merging.
expected_behavior: preflight.sh returns ROUTE=STOP_AMBIGUOUS with REASON naming the closed-unmerged PR
The loop STOPs and reports; it does not reopen the PR, cut a replacement branch, or force a new PR for the same task
The report makes clear that only the operator can decide what happens next

evaluations.name: all-done-ends-the-loop
evaluations.query: Continue the walrus roadmap until it's finished.
evaluations.setup: All 367 roadmap rows, including the fully audited and activated 265-row Rust curriculum, are ✅.
expected_behavior: next_task.py returns VERDICT=ALL_DONE (exit 2)
The loop ends with a final report: the session ledger plus `next_task.py --status` counts
No branch is cut, no PR is opened, and no roadmap file is edited
